concept_definition: In chess, a file is a vertical column of squares running from one side of the board to the other.
In chess, a rank is a horizontal row of eight squares on the board, numbered from 1 to 8.
In chess, a diagonal is a slanting line of squares of the same color that touch at their corners.
In basketball, the paint is the marked area of the court near the basket, extending from the baseline to the free-throw line.
In tennis, the service line is the line across each side of the court that marks the back of the service box.
In tennis, a service box is one of the two marked areas on either side of the net into which a serve must land.
In baseball, the infield is the area inside the four bases, where the pitcher and infielders play.
In baseball, the outfield is the grassy area beyond the infield, where the left, center, and right fielders play.
In baseball, one of the four marked stations that a runner must touch while advancing around the field.
The five-sided rubber plate in baseball where the batter stands and runners must touch to score a run.
In baseball, first base is the first of the four bases that a runner must reach after batting.
In baseball, second base is the base on the right side of the infield from the batter's perspective, opposite home plate and between first and third base.
In baseball, third base is the base a runner reaches after second base and before running to home plate.
In baseball, the mound is the raised area in the center of the diamond where the pitcher stands to deliver the ball.

In baseball, the strike zone is the area over home plate through which a pitch must pass, between the batter’s knees and the midpoint of the torso, to be called a strike when the batter does not swing.
In cricket, a crease is one of the marked lines on the pitch that define where the batter and bowler stand and the limits of their ground.
In cricket, a slip is a close fielding position beside the wicketkeeper, where a fielder stands to catch edges from the batter.
In cricket, a gully is a close fielding position on the off side, behind the batter and beside the slip cordon.
The area at each end of an American football field where a team scores a touchdown by carrying or catching the ball.
A line across an American football field that marks a specific distance in yards from a goal line.
In American football, an imaginary line across the field marking where the ball is placed before a play begins; the two teams must remain on their respective sides until the snap.
In American football, the area between the opponent’s 20-yard line and the goal line, where the offense is close to scoring a touchdown.
The row of squares farthest from a player’s starting side in checkers, where a checker is crowned when it reaches that row.
A designated area in ice hockey where players serve time for penalties.
In ice hockey, either of the two blue lines that divide the rink into the defensive, neutral, and attacking zones.
The red line across the center of an ice hockey rink that divides it into two halves.
A marked area in front of an ice hockey goal where the goaltender plays and opposing players’ actions are restricted by the rules.
A goal left unguarded in ice hockey after a team pulls its goaltender, often allowing the opposing team to score into it.
In golf, one of the numbered sections of a course, usually consisting of a teeing area, a fairway, and a green with a cup, or the cup itself.
The closely mown area of a golf hole between the teeing ground and the green.
In golf, the closely mown, smooth area of grass surrounding the hole, where players putt.
A hollow area on a golf course, usually filled with sand, that is a hazard from which players must play their ball.
An intersection of lines on a Go board where a stone can be placed.
An empty point directly next to a stone or connected group of stones in go, which must be occupied or removed to capture them.
An empty point on a Go board surrounded by one player's stones.
An area of empty intersections on a Go board that a player has surrounded and therefore controls.
The line in rugby that a team must cross with the ball to score a try.
A designated area at one corner of a boxing ring where a boxer rests and receives advice from their team between rounds.
The empty middle row that divides the two sides of a xiangqi board.
In xiangqi, the palace is the three-by-three area on a player's side of the board where that player's general must remain.
A line on a volleyball court three meters from and parallel to the net, separating the front zone from the back zone.
In poker, the fifth and final community card dealt face up in games such as Texas hold’em and Omaha.
One of the 24 long triangles on a backgammon board, where checkers can be placed and moved.
The raised strip across the middle of a backgammon board where hit checkers are placed until they can re-enter.
The quadrant of a backgammon board where a player must move all their checkers before bearing them off.
A row of six consecutive points occupied by one player's checkers, blocking the opponent's checkers from passing in backgammon.
A point in the opponent’s home board occupied by two of a player’s checkers in backgammon.
The marked area in front of each goal on a soccer field where the goalkeeper may handle the ball and certain fouls result in a penalty kick.
In association football, the penalty spot is the marked point from which a penalty kick is taken.
The middle area of an association football pitch, or the group of players who play in that area.
In association football, either of the two boundary lines running along the long sides of the pitch.
the area or part that is at the back of something; the rear side or position
the cardinal direction toward the point of the horizon where the sun rises; the eastern part of a region or country
the inner surface or area of something; the interior part or space within an object or structure
the direction or point on the horizon at 0° on a compass; the region or area that lies toward the North Pole from a given location
The direction halfway between north and east, or the region lying in it.
The direction halfway between north and west, or the region lying in it.
the external area beyond the boundaries of a building or structure; the outdoors
the direction toward the point of the horizon 90° clockwise from east; the cardinal point opposite north
The direction halfway between south and east, or the region lying in it.
The direction halfway between south and west, or the region lying in it.
the direction toward the point of the horizon where the sun sets; the cardinal point opposite east
A distinct part or division of something, especially an area, organization, or economy.
One of the parts into which something is divided.
The way people or things are positioned or organized in a group or structure.
The central or innermost part of something.
The outer limits or peripheral parts of a group, activity, or situation.
A designated space or area where a vehicle may be left temporarily.
A barrier is something that blocks or restricts the movement or spread of something.
In golf, a hazard is an area such as a bunker or water feature that makes play more difficult and may incur a penalty.
The lower or bottom surface of something.
A sloping surface or path that goes downward.
The point at which light or other waves converge, or from which they appear to diverge, where an image is sharp.
A long, narrow trench cut in the soil by a plough when preparing a field for planting.
An imaginary great circle around Earth, equally distant from the North and South Poles, dividing the planet into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres; also, the corresponding line of latitude at 0°.
Either half of the Earth, divided by the equator into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres or by a meridian into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
The top or highest part of something, especially a hill, wave, or roof.
A border or boundary between countries, regions, or territories.
At the rear end of a ship or boat.
An empty space or completely unoccupied area.
An inclined or sloping position, or the act of leaning or inclining.
The highest point or top of something, especially a pointed or roughly conical object.
A hollow space or hole inside something, especially the body or a solid object.
A point at which lines or pathways meet or branch, especially in a network or diagram.
The arrangement of people, objects, or parts in a straight line or in correct relative positions.
The arrangement of text or other visual elements relative to a margin, line, or reference point.
The way the parts of something are arranged or organized, especially on a page, screen, or in a space.
The blank space along the edge of a page or other printed or written surface.
The edge or boundary of an area, especially a place bordering a larger area.
A long, narrow raised strip or projecting line on a surface or object.
The place, conditions, and things around a person, animal, or object; the environment or immediate area.
A point or place where separate things, parts, or systems join or connect.
A place or position from which someone has a good view, especially a high or advantageous one.
One of a series of rows, levels, or layers arranged one above another or in steps; also, one of the levels in a hierarchy or ranking.
An edge or border, especially a narrow strip of ground along a road or path.
The inner part or space of something, especially a building, vehicle, or enclosed area.
A thickness or level of material, substance, or items lying over or under another; one of several such levels.
The angular distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees; also, a line or region sharing the same such distance.
An imaginary great circle on the Earth or a celestial body that passes through both poles; lines of longitude are measured as meridians.
A section of a curved path or trajectory, especially the path followed by a projectile.
A curved part of a circle's circumference.
A turn or change in the direction of a route or course.
The outer surface or part of something, especially a building or object.
A strip or area of land separating the lanes of a divided road.
The curved path followed by an object moving through space, especially when affected by gravity or another force.
A recessed or marked-off area within a larger space, such as a section of a building, room, or vehicle.
A space left empty in a document, form, or text, intended to be filled in.
The way a person stands, especially the position of their feet and body.
One of the parts into which something is divided or naturally separates.
An imaginary straight line around which a body rotates or is considered to rotate.
A central line or structure around which something is arranged, organized, or develops.
A vertical arrangement of objects, numbers, or other items, especially one section of a table or page.
A vertical division of text on a page, separated from another division by space or a line.
A section of a large store devoted to a particular type of merchandise.
A distinct area or range in which something exists, operates, or is valid.
An empty space or opening between two things or parts.
An opening in a line of people, vehicles, or objects that allows passage or provides an opportunity to move through.
The back or opposite side of something, especially a coin, medal, or document.
One of the divisions of the Earth or another planet used to group places with the same standard time.
A band or layer of a particular kind, especially one identified by its depth, position, or natural conditions.
The outermost or most distant point, edge, or part of something.
The side of something, especially a mountain, building, or formation of people or military forces.
A secure position or grip for the feet, especially while standing or moving.
A sunken or lower area in a surface; a hollow or dip.
A space or distance between two things, points, or places.
The curved path followed by a celestial body, satellite, or spacecraft as it moves around another body under gravity.
The region or sphere of activity, influence, or interest within which a person, group, or thing operates.
The position or direction in which something is set or faces, especially in relation to the points of a compass or another reference point.
The back part of something, especially the part opposite its front.
The arrangement or amount of space between things, letters, words, lines, or other elements.
